reader.requirement: At 85, the FILE STATUS operand data-name-1 may be written qualified (IN/OF, several levels). The qualified reference must bind to the item it names and that item must receive the I-O status; an ambiguous unqualified or wrongly qualified name must be refused, and a subscript or reference modifier must be refused because data-name-1 is a data-name.

edition-consulted.switches: EditionInfo.SubscriptedClauseOperands (Year == 2002) admits a subscript on the operand at 2002 only; 85 refuses it, as 2023 does
the same flag decides whether subscripts are kept (2002) or empty
the same flag skips the OCCURS screen at 2002 only

reader.edition-search: grep for SubscriptedClauseOperands, Year and DialectLevel in DataBinder.cs, FileControlBinder.cs and FileControlBinder.Resolve.cs. The qualification walk itself reads no edition
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no between 85 and 2023. 2002 alone admits a subscripted operand
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf10_06 covers one-level qualification at run time. It does not cover multi-level qualification, a status after a failed OPEN, or the refusals

probes.printed: OPEN F1 35 YY WW / READ F1 47 / OPEN F2 00 47 / WRITE F2 00 / CLOSE F2 00
probes.expected: FS OF G-A gets 35 on OPEN INPUT of a missing file and 47 on the READ after the failed open; FS IN INNER IN G-B (two levels) gets 00 on OPEN/WRITE/CLOSE; same-named decoys unchanged

probes.printed: COBOL1639: FILE STATUS 'FS' does not uniquely identify a data item
probes.expected: an ambiguous unqualified name is refused

probes.printed: COBOL1639: 'FS OF G-C' references no data item
COBOL1639: 'FS OF FW' references no data item
probes.expected: refused: the qualifier is not an ancestor

probes.printed: COBOL1639: 'FS OF G-A OF G-B' references no data item
probes.expected: refused: the qualifiers are in different hierarchies

probes.printed: COBOL2024: FILE STATUS 'FT(1)' is written with a subscript (at --std 2002: EXIT 0)
probes.expected: refused at 85, where data-name-1 is a data-name; the 2002 arm admits it

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.2.5.3 SR1  (2.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: Qualification goes through the one ResolveClauseOperand resolver. At 85 the operand takes the same arm as at 2023 (SubscriptedClauseOperands is false). A first probe draft also had a level-01 FS beside two subordinate FS items; it was refused as ambiguous (COBOL1639), and that probe was rewritten.

refuter.evidence: r4a.cob (runs/r4a-002): FILE STATUS IS FS OF GG in a contained program, where 01 GG GLOBAL / 05 MID / 10 FS lives in the containing program, gets 35 on OPEN INPUT of a missing file, seen as 35 by both programs; a separately compiled subprogram with FILE STATUS IS LFS IN L-GRP (a LINKAGE SECTION group passed BY REFERENCE) beside a WORKING-STORAGE decoy W-GRP.LFS sets the caller's item to 00 while the decoy stays WW. r4b.cob (runs/r4b-001): FS OF G-B with FS three levels down (G-B/INNER/DEEP), intermediate qualifiers skipped, gets 35 and the decoy FS OF G-A stays AA. r4c.cob (runs/r4c-001): FS OF F1 (a file-name qualifier, impossible since SR2 bars the File Section) refused COBOL1639. A first r4a draft also had OTHER-G.FS beside the GLOBAL FS; COBOL6862 refused it at the time, and kb/Work PB5629 reversed that: the global attribute of §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 SR4 belongs to the item the GLOBAL clause is on (the 01 record), its subordinates being global names (§1985:X.4.6.4 GR1), so FS and OTHER-G.FS are told apart by qualification and the draft is accepted (conformance:cases/13.18.27-GLOBAL/pb5629_global_subordinate_names_told_apart_by_qualification). cite: OK  §1985:VII.2.5.3 SR1  (2.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1; OK  §1985:VII.2.5.3 SR2  the text is in SR2.
